examples.title: Following a bad sample over the stated task
examples.commentary: The candidate identifies the valid result, then hardcodes the contradictory sample output. This is a concrete example of prompt defects propagating into the answer.

examples.title: A missing physical parameter becomes invented code
examples.commentary: The prompt omits drag strength. The reviewer flags a response that substitutes constant velocities fitted to the example instead of the requested trajectory model.

examples.title: A tool action is exported as the final answer
examples.commentary: A repository listing can be a valid next action in an agent trajectory. In this flattened standalone record, it does not deliver the requested code fix.

examples.title: A correct conclusion can still sit in a flagged record
examples.commentary: The candidate notices that two planes intersect in a line, not a solid. The reviewer nevertheless flags the contradictory premise and repetitive trace. Major flags are not synonymous with wrong final answers.

examples.title: A concrete counterexample to generated code
examples.commentary: The reviewer identifies a minus sign applied to only one regex alternative, and supplies a negative-range counterexample. This is static reviewer reasoning, not an executed test.

examples.title: An outline replaces the requested deliverable
examples.commentary: The Chinese prompt asks for a 3,000-character literature review. The reviewer flags the response for supplying an outline and expansion advice instead.

examples.title: A straightforward usable example
examples.commentary: The chair-count question gives all necessary inputs. The response computes 2 × 6 + 2 × 7 = 26 and the reviewer finds no defect. This example is illustrative, not evidence of broader learning gains.

examples.title: Unverifiable bibliography remains uncertain
examples.commentary: The reviewer cannot establish the asserted historical publications. It records uncertainty rather than treating plausible specificity as evidence.

method.weighted_interval: 95% normal interval using stratified SRS without replacement variance; finite population correction in each source
method.source_interval: 95% Wilson binomial approximation; no finite-population correction
method.caveat: Intervals quantify record sampling uncertainty conditional on model labels; they exclude reviewer error and are not familywise-adjusted comparisons.
